description: Declare clean/test/all as .PHONY, so make still runs them even when a same-named file exists in the directory (a stale artifact currently makes 'make clean' silently do nothing)
prompts: The Makefile's clean and test targets are not declared .PHONY - Make treats a target as a FILE to build by default, so if a file literally named `clean` or `test` ever exists in the directory (e.g. left over from an old build script, or created by a typo), `make clean` / `make test` will see that file already exists with no newer prerequisites and silently do NOTHING instead of running the recipe. Add a `.PHONY: all clean test` declaration covering all three non-file targets (all, clean, test). Keep every existing recipe and target behavior otherwise unchanged.

setup_files.Makefile:
CC = gcc
CFLAGS = -Wall

all: app

app: main.o
	$(CC) -o app main.o

%.o: %.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

test: app
	./app > test_output.txt

clean:
	rm -f app *.o test_output.txt

test_setup_files.test_phony.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

r = subprocess.run(['make', 'all'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'make all failed: {r.stderr}'
assert Path('app').exists(), 'app was not built'

# Simulate the exact failure mode: a stray file literally named 'clean'.
Path('clean').write_text('stray leftover file, not a real target\n', encoding='utf-8')

r = subprocess.run(['make', 'clean'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'make clean failed: {r.stderr}'
assert not Path('app').exists(), (
    'make clean did not actually remove app - a stray file named "clean" fooled it into a no-op '
    '(clean is not declared .PHONY)')

# Rebuild, then check the same failure mode for 'test'.
r = subprocess.run(['make', 'all'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'rebuild failed: {r.stderr}'
Path('test').write_text('stray leftover file, not a real target\n', encoding='utf-8')
Path('test_output.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)

r = subprocess.run(['make', 'test'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'make test failed: {r.stderr}'
assert Path('test_output.txt').exists(), (
    'make test did not actually run - a stray file named "test" fooled it into a no-op '
    '(test is not declared .PHONY)')

print('PASS')

reference_solution.Makefile:
CC = gcc
CFLAGS = -Wall

.PHONY: all clean test

all: app

app: main.o
	$(CC) -o app main.o

%.o: %.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

test: app
	./app > test_output.txt

clean:
	rm -f app *.o test_output.txt
